posts.title: Little Angels + Luke Morley @ KK’s Steel Mill, Wolverhampton – Saturday 21st November 2026
posts.description: KK’s Steel Mill is bursting at the seams tonight for what is one of many sold out shows across the country on Little Angels ‘ Big Bad & Back tour. The interest is understandable as these are the first dates since their brief return in 2012/13, and their first dates in over 30 years to feature new material. They also counldn’t have picked a better suited support than Luke Morley to open the show. Luke Morley – KK’s Steel Mill, Wolverhampton – 21st November 2026 Luke Morley was here a couple of years ago promoting his then new Songs From The Blue Room album. While Chris Childs and Dean Howard remain these dates are completed by Willie Dowling on keys and Darby Todd on drums and it seem a far more rockier affair. ‘I Wanna See The Light’ kicks things off and ‘Snakeskin Parachute’ is a slice of pure rock ‘n’ roll. posts.title: Interview with Sweet Crystal!
posts.description: Hailing from the tough-as-nails city of Detroit, Sweet Crystal have been charting their own course for over half a century, picking up a host of awards along the way (see below). It’s a journey that hasn’t always been easy but the band’s belief and convictions have ensured their ship has remained steady. With very little help from the mainstream media, Sweet Crystal might just be the biggest band you’ve never heard on national radio. It’s time to set that right, so we were delighted to speak to lead vocalist and keyboardist MarQ Andrew Speck: Can you tell us about the band’s origins. Where did you meet etc. Ready for a long tale some 5 decades in the making? Seriously, the three of us that started SWEET CRYSTAL (myself [MarQ Andrew Speck] on keys and lead vocals, Bill Blatter on guitars and Steve Wieser on drums) began this musical mission right out of high school as we started our college years. posts.title: Molly Hatchet – Lost Horizon
posts.description: Originally formed in Jacksonville, Florida, in 1971, Molly Hatchet have had a line-up that’s been in constant flux. With no original members remaining since their first album (1978’s self-titled effort), a Molly Hatchet album isn’t so much about the personnel, more the feel and aesthetic of those records and how they stay true to the band’s original vision whilst moving the band forwards. It’s a fine line that needs to be walked and one that Bobby Ingram (guitar) and John Galvin (keyboards) have traversed since 1989 (with help from long term bassist Tim Lindsey) and is continued on latest album Lost Horizon . Featuring a dozen tracks that blur the line between Southern, blues, boogie and hard rock, this is an album that pays homage to the band’s illustrious past whilst setting their sights firmly on the future.
